entry.title: Crucible Rankings Season 1 Concludes Soon & Season 2 Start Date Announced
entry.summary:
We would like to announce the end date for Season 1 of the Crucible Rankings.

Season 1 Ranking Period End Date

Monday, November 30, 2026 at 8:59 p.m. (PST)

Upon conclusion of the season, players who rank in the top 300 of their physical data center will receive ranking rewards.

The season will soon come to a close. Push for the top of the rankings alongside your trusty companions!

View the Crucible Rankings and rewards here.

Once Season 1 concludes, a pre-season period will begin, during which players will be unable to participate in Crucible Rankings. Season 2 is scheduled to commence on Monday, December 7, 2026 at 9:00 p.m. (PST).

Season 2 Ranking Period

Monday, December 7, 2026 at 9:00 p.m. (PST) until the start of maintenance for Patch 8.0
* Dates and times are subject to change.

entry.title: Letter from the Producer, LXV: The Road to Evercold Promotion
entry.summary:
In a new Letter from the Producer, Naoki Yoshida discusses the upcoming Road to Evercold promotion.

Read over the complete letter.
entry.content:
Hello, Warriors of Light!
This is Producer & Director Naoki Yoshida.
I can hardly remember the last time I did a Letter from the Producer that wasn't LIVE... (lol)

The reason I'm writing this is because of the upcoming Road to Evercold promotion beginning on November 16. This promotion features certain initiatives which we intentionally refrained from implementing until now, so I thought it prudent to speak with you about them.

What's this promotion all about?

Simply put, the Road to Evercold is a way to encourage any Warrior of Light currently taking a break from their adventures to jump back into the fray before the new expansion arrives. We've held promotions of this nature before, both on a seasonal basis and ahead of expansion releases.

For MMORPGs─especially those with a monthly subscription fee─retaining active players is of utmost importance. This is why the FFXIV Development and Operations teams continually strive to update the in-game universe, add new content, and provide an ever-expanding adventure for our Warriors of Light.

To keep an MMORPG going and growing, in addition to supporting our current players, it's vital that we also welcome new players into the fold, as well as ensure adventurers on a break can readily resume their journey.

That said, encouraging players to return is no mean feat. People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today. (Please bear with me regarding auto-demolition for housing, a symptom of the issues surrounding plots…)

Over the course of three years, for example, middle school students become high school students, and high school students are faced with the decision of going to college or entering the workforce. College juniors are likely beginning their search for employment, while working professionals may be considering whether to stay at their first company or look for a new job. Some people may be starting families, while others are facing job transfers, or even moving residences and temporarily losing internet access—there are countless reasons why people may choose to take a break from gaming.

With these cycles growing ever shorter, it's crucial that we run promotions to help those players toying with the idea of returning to Eorzea, and give them the tiny nudge they might need to dive back in.

Of course, it's all of you who are actively continuing your adventures that we consider the most important. You are always our priority when it comes to developing patches and expansions. That said, "massively multiplayer" is at the heart of the MMORPG experience, which is precisely why doing our best to reach all of our Warriors of Light is our major focus for FFXIV.

Why introduce the promotion now?

As I've mentioned at our Fan Festivals, FFXIV is undertaking a major challenge as we aim to reach a brand-new phase. With the theme of evolution at the forefront, we're expanding and adjusting systems, user interfaces, and content in a way we've never attempted before. My biggest wish is that players currently taking a break will see Evercold as the perfect time to return.

Catching Up in an MMORPG

Whether you're starting an MMORPG or picking up where you left off, the time commitment required to get up to speed and catch up with other players can seem daunting. Newcomers and returning players will naturally have varying views based on how familiar they are with the game, but the perceived hurdles remain for both groups.

Though we endeavor to facilitate this catch-up process through our game design, everyone values their time differently, and some may be demotivated by the hurdles they perceive.

In fact, I'm asked about this wherever and whenever I give interviews. "The story is lauded but so lengthy. Do you really expect players to go through it all from the beginning?" "Why don't you make it easier to catch up and start our adventures from the latest point in the story?"

I've played all kinds of MMORPGs since the genre's early days, and now I'm a developer myself. While I understand where these interview questions are coming from, I strongly believe that FFXIV is a story-driven MMORPG. On top of that, skipping it all means you likely won't be familiar with the battle system and therefore will become a burden for other players in multiplayer content. This is precisely why Tales of Adventure has remained a paid item, with the idea that the expense would dissuade all but the most determined and motivated players from skipping through the story.

Having said this, the Hydaelyn & Zodiark saga alone encompasses five expansions' worth of content: A Realm Reborn, Heavensward, Stormblood, Shadowbringers, and Endwalker. And with Dawntrail marking the start of the second saga, plus the coming addition of Evercold, the story continues to unfold into something even larger.

The idea of letting players freely choose a starting point for their adventure has been discussed, with the goal being to offer players a range of choices, rather than prescribe their experience according to my philosophy. With New Game+ working smoothly, this approach could indeed work. In fact, we'd been laying groundwork to make this a possibility in conjunction with the release of the Nintendo Switch™ 2 version, but ultimately decided to postpone this initiative.

Preparing to Give Players More Options

We welcomed an influx of new Warriors of Light from across the world with the release of FFXIV on XBOX and Switch 2. Seeing players share their positive experiences on social media, and watching veteran players help eager sprouts on their adventures reaffirmed my thinking—that we should avoid measures that might damage this aspect of the community.

Even if you could start adventuring from a point of your choosing, the time and effort required to master a job remain a constant. We also need to avoid situations where both new and veteran players are left confused when matched together. However, with all these considerations in mind, we've held meetings to discuss system and tutorial improvements, and have set ourselves a significant goal for the future. Although we'll need more time to realize this goal, I think giving players more freedom in their adventures will ultimately prove a positive change.

Experiencing Evercold

Even though the changes I've just discussed are still in the works, I still want players to experience Evercold nonetheless! (I am the Producer & Director, after all...) And so, having determined they would serve as a touchstone when considering future approaches, we arrived at the Road to Evercold, which features our longest Free Login Campaign to date and the introduction of "Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude."

Although "Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude" will be available for a limited time and at a discounted price, it is nonetheless a paid item. Additionally, players must have completed Endwalker to use it. In other words, anyone doing so will have attained level 90 in at least one job, be familiar with matching, and be well-experienced in battle. My hope is that players who have completed the game's first saga, but are currently taking a break, will seize this chance to see how FFXIV has evolved.

One option for players using "Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude" is to enjoy the latest chapter of the story before using New Game+ to go back and experience the narrative at their leisure. Hopefully this will inspire Warriors of Light considering a return to Eorzea and beyond to pick up the mantle once again.

Looking Ahead

Sixteen years have passed since the game launched, and thirteen years since A Realm Reborn was released, but FFXIV's journey is not yet complete—its world is still expanding, its narrative still flowing onward. Our mission is twofold: to continue making this grand adventure, and to invite new players to the rich world we've created. And that's why we'll keep on striving to ensure FFXIV is always fresh and exciting, and remains a world which brings happiness to all our wonderful players!

I hope you'll be with us for the next step in FINAL FANTASY XIV's journey!

In the meantime, it's time for the final push to bring Evercold to life!

FINAL FANTASY XIV Producer & Director

Naoki Yoshida

entry.title: The Road to Evercold Promotion Begins Today!
entry.summary:
The Road to Evercold begins today, helping you prepare for the upcoming release of Evercold!

  • Our longest Free Login Campaign ever! Play free up to 30 days!
  • Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude available for a limited time!

A new Letter from the Producer from Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida has been published to mark the start of the promotion—be sure to check it out!

Visit the Road to Evercold special site for details.
